body.statement: For all \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) with \(\mathsf S(C)\neq\mathsf S(D)\), \(\mathsf{Route}(C,D)\) returns \(E\in\{C,D\}\), \(J\in\{C,D\}\setminus\{E\}\), \(z\in V\), and \(\mathcal A_z\subseteq\Pi^E_z\) with \(1\leq|\mathcal A_z|\leq2\). With every innovation variance equal to one, every block coefficient in \(E\) equal to one on \(\mathcal A_z\) and zero elsewhere, and \(A_z=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal A_z}B\), the resulting covariance satisfies \[B^{\star}=e_z\mathbf 1_{A_z}^{\mathsf T},\qquad (B^{\star})^2=0,\qquad \Sigma^{\star}=(I_p+B^{\star})(I_p+B^{\star})^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal M(E)\setminus\mathcal M(J).\] Every entry of \(\Sigma^{\star}\) is an integer in \(\{0,1,\ldots,p\}\), \(\det(\Sigma^{\star})=1\), and the router returns either an ordered certificate \(f_{uvS}(\Sigma^{\star})\) or a blocked-regression certificate \(L_{j;u,v}(\Sigma^{\star})\) whose value belongs to \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). Every recovered regression coefficient in the certificate has numerator in \(\{-1,0,1\}\) and reduced denominator at most \(p\), so all supplied numerical data have height at most \(B(p)=\lceil\log_2p\rceil\). The route uses polynomially many graph and rational-arithmetic operations in \(p\). For \(p=1\), the implication is vacuous.
body.justification: This is the citation-independent necessity bridge: every inequivalent signature receives a sparse, bounded, exactly checkable observable witness.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 19 and Question 20, gives proper-blocked identifiability and an ideal-based equivalence test but no bounded witness theorem; SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 give determinant-vanishing machinery without coefficient-colour height guarantees.
body.consumer: A coloured-DAG solver can return a short certificate explaining why two fitted causal-community states are observationally inequivalent.
